item.title: Version 1.8.0-beta.1
item.description:
SupaSidebar 1.8.0-beta.1

What’s New

  • Not Responding Notice - When a browser stops answering, Live Tabs now says so and keeps its last tabs on screen, dimmed.
  • Try Again for a Frozen Browser - Switching to a profile Space whose browser is frozen leaves its windows alone and offers Try again.
  • Blocked Profiles on macOS 27 - When macOS 27 blocks Chrome, Brave, Edge or Firefox profiles, the picker keeps them and shows how to allow access.
  • Dia Profiles - Link Spaces to Dia profiles and open links in the Dia profile you pick.
  • Make Room for Stage Manager - With Stage Manager on, the sidebar keeps clear of the recent apps strip, and a tip offers to turn off that edge’s trigger.
  • Use Icon Services - A new switch in About, Privacy stops icon lookups through DuckDuckGo and Google, for networks that block them.
  • Route Links by App - With SupaSidebar as your default browser, Air Traffic Control can route links by the app you clicked them in.
  • Domain and Regex Routes - Air Traffic Control routes can now match a whole domain or a regular expression.
  • Test a Link - Paste a link into Air Traffic Control to see which route opens it and where.
  • Skip SupaView for a Route - A route can now open its links straight in your browser instead of SupaView.
  • SupaView Address Bar - Click a SupaView page’s title or press ⌘L to edit its address in the Command Panel.
  • Copy URL in SupaView - Copy a SupaView page’s link from the icon in its URL bar or with ⌘⇧C.

Improvements

  • Open All in One Profile Window - In a Space linked to a browser profile, Open All puts every page in one window of that profile.
  • New Windows Use the Linked Profile - Open in New Window and ⌘N now open in the Space’s linked profile, and the menu names it.
  • Hover Delay Down to 0s - Set Hover Delay to 0s and the sidebar appears the moment your cursor reaches the screen edge.
  • Room Past the Last Live Tab - Live Tabs now scrolls a little past the last tab, so it no longer sits against the bottom bar.
  • Clearer Linked Profile Loading - Live Tabs now says when it’s opening a window or loading its tabs, and why a list is empty.
  • Onboarding Built Around Your Browser - New users get ⌃Tab on its own screen, and the Command Panel and browser keys screens show what each one replaces.
  • Simpler Route Editor - The Air Traffic Control route editor now reads as one sentence, with an example for each match type.
  • Find New Profiles From the Editor - A refresh button next to Open in picks up browser profiles you added after SupaSidebar started.
  • Open in Says Why - SupaView’s Open in button now names the browser and profile it will use and why.

Bug Fixes

  • The Command Panel no longer gets stuck as a thin strip on macOS 26 and 27.
  • Auto-hide no longer stops working until a relaunch after Safari freezes.
  • Live Tabs no longer goes empty when a slow Safari has many tabs open.
  • Dia windows in Live Tabs now keep their numbers when you switch between them.
  • Switching to a Space linked to a closed browser profile now brings its new window to the front and loads its tabs.
  • Clicking another browser after closing a linked profile’s window now switches to that browser’s Space.
  • Closing a linked profile’s window with ⌘W now brings the sidebar back and switches to the Space of the window behind it.
  • Closing Live Tabs at the end of a scrolled list now slides the next tab under your pointer instead of the one above it.
  • With Stage Manager on, clicking a Live Tab in a minimized window now brings that window to the front.
  • Grant Access now adds SupaSidebar to the Accessibility list, so you no longer have to add it with +.
  • Switching to SupaSidebar with Settings open no longer freezes it for several seconds.
  • A Command Panel search in a Safari profile now opens in the window in front instead of one behind it.
  • Opening a SupaView page in your browser now keeps its sign-in and deep-link details, so logins no longer break.
  • Websites can no longer send commands to SupaSidebar’s MCP connection, which now requires a private access key.

Performance

  • Instant Command Panel - The Command Panel now opens in about 40 ms, down from about 230 ms, and closes instantly.
  • Faster Current-Tab Highlight - The sidebar now marks the tab you switch to in about 60 ms, down from about 250 ms.
  • No Stalls From a Frozen Browser - A browser that stops responding no longer holds up Smart Attach, auto-hide or the sidebar for seconds.
  • Faster Safari Live Tabs - Safari with 150 tabs open now loads in under a second instead of up to 7 seconds.
  • Lighter Safari Profile Spaces - Switching tabs in a Space linked to a Safari profile no longer asks Safari for its window list each time.
  • Lighter Folder List - Sidebars with many folders now do less work each time the list redraws.
  • Browser Icons Load in the Background - The first sidebar open no longer waits for browser icons to load from disk.

Notes

  • If an AI app reaches SupaSidebar through MCP, update supasidebar-mcp to 0.2.4 or later, since older versions can no longer connect.
